text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ADEVARUL
- Parliment will discuss bill on bank privatisation in emergency procedure.
- High tariffs for railway fares cuts number of passengers.
- High prices and poverty force many Romanians to sell their gold jewellery.
- Romania will have good wheat and rye crops this year, the paper quotes an Agriculture Ministry official as saying.
- Workers at the Roman SA truck factory started talks with government officials to settle labour conflict started on Monday.
- Prosecutors started to investigate the way local businessman George Paunescu got a $10 million credit to aquire a 31 percent stake in the Bankoop SA commercial bank.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- The Craiova-based Daewoo Automobile SA car maker exported the first batch of 144 Cielo cars to Poland.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- The government approved cuts in import taxes for farm products.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Thosands of workers at the Brasov-based truck maker Roman SA blocked roads in protest of the government's reform programme.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Bookshops in the northern town of Botosani sell books with payments in instalments due to a drop in buyers' living standards.
- Some 100,000 people study in Romania's 44 private universities.
- Budapest sees the European Union extending to include Hungary but not Romania, the newspaper says quoting Hungarian parliament chairman Zoltan Gal.
ADEVARUL
- Nationalist Cluj mayor Gheorghe Funar declined an offer to join the Greater Romania Party as secretary general.
- President Emil Constantinescu met government members and leaders of the ruling coalition to ask them to speed up reform measures and to point out delays in implementing programmes.

- Human rights monitoring by the Council of Europe could be terminated for Romania starting April 24 after the Council's rapporteur Gunnar Jansson's related details on the country's democratic progress since last November elections.
- People queue to sell jewellery to get money for food and medicine, the newspaper says.
- Romania wastes some 22 percent of its water due to poor pipes. The loss is worth an annual $650 million.
- Daewoo Automobile Romania SA car maker sent all its employees on forced holidays due to dropping sales. Unions threatened to turn up at the plant, the newspaper says.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Paunescu denies he was heard by prosecutors in the case of his Bankcoop share acquisition, saying it was "mere talk".

- Paunescu's lawyer Ioan Mustata slams the police and prosecutors for alleged illegal actions against his client, saying they did not press official charges. ($= 7,021 lei) -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
